fichas.title: Museum: General Functional Scheme
fichas.summary: A museum collects, documents, receives, researches, interprets, and communicates objects that testify to human cultural development. The functional scheme distinguishes public controlled areas, exhibition spaces, administration, and restoration areas, with separate visitor and artwork delivery access. Museum types are described by the origins and nature of their collections.
uses: Providing visitor amenities and public facilities
Cataloguing, copying, and archiving collection information
Receiving and delivering works of art

fichas.title: Museum Display Lighting
fichas.summary: Museum display objects should be protected from direct daylight and ultraviolet radiation. Display rooms need flexible lighting without permanently built-in or fixed wall and ceiling lights, and must be capable of complete darkening. The page illustrates indirect and north-facing daylighting approaches and gives illumination guidance by object sensitivity.
uses: Illuminating displayed objects while limiting damage
Using filtered indirect light or north-facing roof and side lighting
Darkening display rooms completely when required

fichas.title: Museum Store and Display Room Climate
fichas.summary: Climate recommendations vary by collection material and season. Store and display temperatures are specified for winter and summer, with an upper summer limit; cooler conditions are recommended for insect-sensitive collections and photographic materials. Relative humidity targets differ by material, and rapid or seasonal humidity fluctuations should be limited.
uses: Preserving stored and displayed collections through temperature and humidity control
Reducing insect reproduction in science and ethnography collections
Storing photographic and film materials in cool, dry conditions
